result:
Done. The change request is fully implemented, tested, and committed.

## What I built

**`GET /users`** (admin only) — returns all users as `{ id, name, email, role }`.

**`PATCH /users/:id/role`** (admin only) — accepts `{"role": "admin"}` or `{"role": "member"}` and changes the user's role.

## Key design decisions

- **Immediate effect for signed-in users.** The bearer token embeds the role at login time, so trusting it would mean a demoted/promoted user keeps their old privileges until re-login. I changed `requireAuth` to resolve the role from the database on every request (`findUserById`). A promotion or demotion now applies on the very next request, even with an already-issued token — covered by two dedicated tests.

- **Last admin protection.** `changeUserRole` rejects demoting an admin to member when they're the only admin (`countAdmins() === 1`), returning `409 E_CONFLICT`.

## Conventions followed
- Error envelope via `sendError`/`ApiError` only (`E_VALIDATION`, `E_CONFLICT`, `E_FORBIDDEN`, `E_NOT_FOUND`).
- New `user.schema.js` with a `role` enum; validated in the route before the service runs; unknown fields rejected.
- Strict `routes → services → repositories` layering; SQL stays in `users.repo.js` (added `listUsers`, `updateUserRole`, `countAdmins`).

All 129 tests pass (12 new), `typecheck` and `lint` are clean.
